en: A session cleaned cargo build output from worktrees whose <t1/> mtime was older than 24 hours, to recover a full disk. It computed <t2/>. For three worktrees <t3/> returned nothing because the directory was being written at that exact moment; the shell substituted an empty string for the missing mtime, and the arithmetic on an empty string produced an age of roughly 496938 hours instead of an error. Three active worktrees looked like the oldest, most stale candidates in the set and were cleaned. Only build output was lost, and it rebuilds, but the shape of the bug is general: a script that turns "I could not measure this" into a number treats not-knowing as the strongest possible answer to the question a deletion asks.

Tři aktivní worktree vypadaly jako nejstarší, nejzastaralejší kandidáti v sadě a byly vyčištěny. Přišlo se jen o výstup buildu, který se znovu sestaví, ale tvar chyby je obecný: skript, který mění „nemohl jsem to změřit“ na číslo, bere nevědomost jako nejsilnější možnou odpověď na otázku, kterou smazání klade.

A request from another origin is refused <t4/> before the handshake — a page elsewhere can open a WebSocket to a loopback server, and the same-origin policy does not stop it. So is an upgrade from this machine addressed to a host name that is neither an address nor <t5/>: that is a page whose domain was made to resolve here (DNS rebinding), refused before the upgrade as every other route refuses it. An <t6/> parameter that is not an execution id is <t7/>, refused by shape before anything is looked up.

Stejně tak upgrade z tohoto stroje adresovaný na jméno hostitele, které není ani adresa, ani <t5/>: to je stránka, jejíž doména byla donucena překládat se sem (DNS rebinding), odmítnutá před upgradem, jako ji odmítá každá jiná routa.
